([[Zion, Illinois]]) | college = [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] (2015–2019) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = *[[Associated Press|AP]] Honorable Mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2019 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2019]]) *First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2019) *Second-team All-SEC (2018) }} '''Admiral Schofield''' (born March 30, 1997) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]]. ==Early life== Schofield, the son of Anthony and Dawn Schofield, was born at [[St Mary's Hospital, London|St Mary's Hospital]] in London while his father was stationed there with the [[United States Navy|U.S. Navy]].{{cite web|url=https://utsports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=6752 |title=2018–19 Men's Basketball Roster: Admiral Schofield |publisher=[[Tennessee Volunteers]] |accessdate=January 1, 2019}} {{cite web|url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/badgers/67837037.html|title=An inspirational journey: UW's Schofield motivated after loss of his brother|accessdate=January 20, 2014|date=October 30, 2009|work=[[Journal Sentinel]]|author=Potrykus, Jeff}} His brother [[O'Brien Schofield]] is a linebacker who won a Super Bowl with the [[Seattle Seahawks]]. He has another brother General and a sister Octavia; one other brother, Jordan, drowned in [[Lake Michigan]] in 2007. Admiral Schofield attended [[Zion-Benton High School]] where he played center. In his final high school game, he recorded 23 points with 18 rebounds against Stevenson in the Class 4A regional championship. In [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] play, he competed for Dickey Simpkins' Team NLP. [[Donnie Tyndall]] recruited him to Tennessee, but Schofield decided to stay after Tyndall was fired. ==College career== Schofield averaged 7.6 points and 4.0 rebounds per game as a freshman. He missed three games as a sophomore while he was suspended for violating team rules. He only scored 3.5 points per game in nonconference play, but began to break out during the conference season and had his first double-double of 18 points and 10 rebounds in a loss to [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]].{{cite news|last1=Brown|first1=Patrick|title=Admiral Schofield now playing like Vols 'want and expect|url=http://www.timesfreepress.com/news/sports/college/story/2017/jan/18/admiral-schofield-now-playing-vols-want-and-e/408081/|accessdate=May 20, 2018|work=[[Times Free Press]]|date=January 18, 2017}} As a sophomore at Tennessee, Schofield averaged 8.2 points and 4.4 rebounds per game.{{cite news|last1=Ryan|first1=Shannon|title=Zion-Benton product Admiral Schofield out to help Tennessee sink Loyola|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-loyola-tennessee-admiral-schofield-20180316-story.html|accessdate=May 20, 2018|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=March 17, 2018}} Schofield was named to the SEC All-Tournament Team as a junior due to a 22-point effort in the SEC Title game loss to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{cite news|last1=White|first1=Taylor|title=Schofield declares for draft without hiring agent|url=https://www.thedailytimes.com/test/schofield-declares-for-draft-without-hiring-agent/article_1b2b99b0-bf59-5fc3-be85-74502d13f5bf.html|accessdate=May 20, 2018|work=[[The Daily Times (Blount County, Tennessee)|The Daily Times]]|date=March 30, 2018}} As a junior, Schofield averaged 13.9 points and 6.5 rebounds per game. He helped Tennessee to a 26–9 record and the second round of the NCAA tournament. In the first round win over [[Wright State Raiders men's basketball|Wright State]], Schofield had 15 points and 12 rebounds. Schofield was named to the Second Team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]]. Following the season, he declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent, thus leaving open the possibility of returning to the Volunteers.{{cite news|last1=Toppmeyer|first1=Blake|title=Tennessee Vols forward Admiral Schofield will enter name in NBA draft but won't hire agent|url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2018/03/29/tennessee-vols-basketball-admiral-schofield-nba-draft-agent-rick-barnes-mock-draft-ut-sec-hoops/471409002/|accessdate=May 20, 2018|work=[[Knoxville News-Sentinel]]|date=March 29, 2018}} Schofield announced his return to Tennessee on May 29.{{cite news |last1=Johnson |first1=Raphielle |title=Admiral Schofield’s return sets up Tennessee for big 2018–19 season |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/05/29/admiral-schofields-return-sets-up-tennessee-for-big-2018-19-season/ |accessdate=May 30, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=May 29, 2018}} As a senior, Schofield averaged 16.5 points and 6.1 rebounds per game.{{cite news |title=Grant Williams, Admiral Schofield earn AP All-American honors |url=https://www.wbir.com/article/sports/college/vols/grant-williams-admiral-schofield-earn-ap-all-american-honors/51-4f282e9c-0501-4fa6-b87c-b05012a9c53b |accessdate=April 4, 2019 |work=WBIR |date=April 2, 2019}} He was named to the First Team All-SEC.{{cite press release|url=http://www.secsports.com/article/26238088/2019-sec-men-basketball-awards-announced |title=2019 SEC Men's Basketball Awards announced |publisher=Southeaster Conference |date=March 12, 2019 |accessdate=March 12, 2019}} He led Tennessee to a 31–6 record and the Sweet 16 of the NCAA tournament. In his final career game, a 99-94 overtime loss to [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], Schofield finished with 21 points.{{cite news |title=Elite Eight-bound: Purdue holds off Tennessee 99-94 in OT |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401123382 |accessdate=April 4, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 29, 2019}} ==Career statistics==
